The start and end of the day go well when everyone knows the rhythm. Here is how drop-off and hometime run at The City School, and who may collect your child. The rhythm of the day AM Morning drop-off Bring your child to the gate in the morning and a member of staff walks them in. Your class teacher confirms the exact times for your child's year group. PM Hometime At the end of the day, children are collected from the gate at hometime. Times differ by year group, so your class teacher confirms exact times with you. When times change On the last day of a term, hometime is earlier: this year it is 11:30 for K1 and K2, and 12:00 for Y1 to Y6. Any other change is posted on the status page and shared by your campus. Who can collect your child Authorisation lanyards Your child is released only to an adult carrying an ELC authorisation lanyard for your family. Giving at ELC starts with the children. In the sala, the school's gathering place, they build connections with each other, with their teachers and with the world, and somewhere in that the me becomes a we. The fundraising this community does grows out of exactly that. What this community has done Class artworks on their easels for the Art from the Heart raffle. For Art from the Heart, every class made a collaborative artwork and families bought raffle tickets to take one home. The money raised went to the Pediatric Cardiac Surgery Foundation to fund life-saving heart surgery. Read the story on our blog. Families making together at a charity book and bake day. Charity days here have a familiar shape: children and parents making, baking and selling together, and children learning along the way that privilege carries a duty to others. Read the story on our blog. The giving reaches beyond the school gates too. Families have been invited to stand with the Bookworm Fou

Workshops, social mornings and other events that bring the ELC community together: children and parents. La Comunità is how we turn a school into a place families belong. What these occasions are like Social mornings are the easiest place to start: coffee, no agenda, and other families who walk the same route as you. Their dates live on this page, above. Parent workshops go one layer deeper, bringing a specialist to the questions parents actually carry. One workshop on positive parenting kept returning to a single idea: trust, in yourself as a parent and in your child. Read the story on our blog. The Carnival of Cultures celebrated the many cultures inside this one school community, and parents ran the country pavilions themselves. Read the story on our blog. And Fun Field Day brought the whole school onto the field for a day of games and team spirit, with older children helping younger ones through the course. Read the story on our blog. Map Easy Parking, on Thong Lor 13 A second option if you self-drive: 32 Akkhara Phat Alley, opposite Nihonmura and beside KC Court on soi 49/13. A two minute walk to school. Map SOI The back entrance on soi 53 Drop-off and pick-up only: there is no parking here, and car access beyond soi Renoo is for local residents only. h: What this site knows about you: nothing.
b: ELC Portal v0.8 This week Activities Calendar Centres City School PE 39, 49 & 55 PE Samakee Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary Nuts and bolts This week / Privacy Privacy What this site knows about you: nothing. No login. No accounts. No cookies. No trackers. No child data. This page explains what that means, and where your information does live when you sign up for something. A promise you can check This site is a set of plain pages. It sets no cookies, keeps no accounts, loads no advertising scripts, and serves everything, including its fonts, from its own address. We count which pages get opened so we know what helps; the counter stores the page address, including any campaign tag on a link we sent, and nothing else; there is no cookie, no fingerprint, and nothing that identifies you, and you can verify this in your browser's developer tools. If you install this site as an app, the pages are stored on your own device so they open offline. Only that page-open count is ever sent back to us. Where your information does go Some links on this site take you to the systems that run registration and feedback. Each one only ever holds what you type into it: Registration form

This page is here for the rare moment something feels wrong, but the care behind it runs all year. Every child's safety and wellbeing comes first at ELC, and that is a promise the whole community keeps together, with teachers and families in partnership. Who to speak to Speak to any teacher or the school office, in person or by email: . They will bring in the campus safeguarding lead the same day. Named safeguarding leads for each campus are being added to this page. What happens after you report Your concern goes to the campus safeguarding lead, who decides the next step the same day. h: How to know a message is really from ELC.
The official channels, all of them
b: ELC Portal v0.8 This week Activities Calendar Centres City School PE 39, 49 & 55 PE Samakee Policies FAQ Quick answers New families Glossary Nuts and bolts This week / Is it really us Verify How to know a message is really from ELC. Scammers target school parents in Bangkok, often over LINE, and often about money. Here is how to check any message in ten seconds. The official channels, all of them This site: portal.elc.ac.th The school website: elc.ac.th Email from an address ending @elc.ac.th, and nothing else The Parent App, for your child's learning Three rules that never change We never ask for payment through LINE chat or any other chat message. We never ask you to pay into a personal bank account. School payments go to the school. We never rush you. A real school message survives you taking a day to check it. When something feels off Stop. Pay nothing, click nothing, reply to nothing. Contact the school office yourself, using an address you already know, not one from the suspicious message: Checking a real message costs a minute. Trusting a fake one can cost a term's fees. We would always rather answer a "was this you?" email. portal.elc.ac.th · ELC International Schools, Thon
